instruction: Please create an SSH user named "bob" with password "P@ssw0rd!987" on Ubuntu who is only allowed to access the folder "/home/project1".

result.command: USERNAME="bob"; HOMEDIR="/home/project1"; PASSWORD="P@ssw0rd!987"; ./check_password.sh "$USERNAME" "$PASSWORD" && [ "$(getent passwd "$USERNAME" | cut -d: -f6)" = "$HOMEDIR" ] && [ $(stat -c "%A" "$HOMEDIR" | cut -b 3) = "w" ] && echo "Password, home directory, and write permission check passed" || echo "Check failed"

include: Password, home directory, and write permission check passed

metadata.explanation: Task creates SSH user 'bob' with password 'P@ssw0rd!987' restricted to folder '/home/project1'. Evaluator verifies: (1) SSH password authentication works, (2) home directory is set to /home/project1, (3) user has write permission to the folder.

llm_judge_reasons: CRITICAL: Incomplete verification of core requirement - Instruction requires user 'only allowed to access' /home/project1 (access restriction), but evaluator only checks home directory and write permission, not actual access restriction

The evaluator would pass for unrestricted user with correct home directory - Missing verification of SSH chroot configuration, restricted shell (rssh/scponly), or sshd_config Match user settings with ForceCommand/ChrootDirectory
Semantic mismatch: Evaluator checks 'write permission' but instruction only says 'access' which could be read-only or read-write
The check_password.sh script verifies SSH login works and home directory is set, but does not verify confinement/restriction to that directory
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Add verification for SSH access restriction mechanisms: check sshd_config for ChrootDirectory or Match User block with ForceCommand internal-sftp
Add test to verify user CANNOT access directories outside /home/project1 (e.g., try to cd to /etc or /var and verify failure)
Consider checking for restricted shell in /etc/passwd (user shell should be rssh, scponly, or /usr/sbin/nologin with sftp-only access)
Remove or justify the write permission check if instruction doesn't explicitly require write access
